sources.entry: Laradock | Full PHP development environment based on Docker (Nginx, PHP, MySQL, Redis and more)

summary.one_liner: Laradock is a Docker-based full PHP development environment that runs pre-configured containers (Nginx, PHP-FPM, MySQL, Redis and 100+ other services) for any PHP project.
summary.what_it_does: Laradock is cloned into a PHP project and started with a single command, giving a local stack of containers for the web server, PHP runtime, databases, caches, queues, search, and mail testing. A "Laradock CLI" (./laradock) provides a setup wizard, start/stop-style commands, and a "workspace" shell containing php, composer, node, and git, and unknown commands pass through to docker compose. The README says PHP versions from 5.6 to 8.5 can be selected via PHP_VERSION in .env, and each service can be toggled on or off and configured by overriding settings in .env. It also describes a "ship" command that builds an image for deployment to platforms such as Kubernetes, Cloud Run, or ECS. Plain docker compose usage is supported as an alternative to the CLI.
use_cases: Local development environment for Laravel or other PHP apps
Running Docker-based Nginx, PHP-FPM, and MySQL locally
Running legacy PHP 5.6 or 7.x apps without changing host PHP
Spinning up Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch or other services for a project
Testing outgoing email with Mailpit or Mailhog
Running WordPress, Magento, or Drupal in containers
Running local LLMs with Ollama alongside a PHP app
how_to_run: git clone <laradock repo URL> inside your PHP project (README leaves the URL blank)
./laradock start (first run opens a setup wizard)
Alternatively: docker compose up -d <container-name> and docker compose exec workspace bash
notable: Single-command stack with a setup wizard and pre-configured containers for 100+ services
Workspace container with PHP, Composer, Node, Git and other CLI tools so nothing needs installing on the host
Supports PHP versions from 5.6 to 8.5 selectable through .env
Built-in ./laradock ship command to package the stack for production deployment
CLI is transparent: it prints the docker compose commands it runs
caveats: Requires Docker with Compose v2.20 or newer
Sponsorship is requested for ongoing maintenance; the README does not describe paid tiers
Several services (such as Jenkins, GitLab, SonarQube) are heavy to run locally, though the README does not state resource requirements
keywords: set up php project in docker
local development stack for php apps
